title: Out shopping
why: The lesson takes the learner shopping: clothing and shoe sizes, trying things on (¿Puedo probármelo?), saying how something fits with quedar, choosing with este, ese, aquel, paying, returning and exchanging. It recycles attached pronouns and comparatives just before the big A2 review.

{"lessons": ["

In the store: asking and trying on

In Spain, the salesperson (el dependiente, la dependienta) often speaks to you with tú, especially in clothing stores. You can do the same, or use usted in a more traditional shop.

You want to…You sayTranslation
ask for an item¿Tienen esta camisa en la talla 40?Do you have this shirt in a size 40?
another color¿La tenéis en azul?Do you have it in blue?
another size¿Tienes una talla más? / ¿Una talla menos?Do you have one size up? / One size down?
shoesCalzo un 39. ¿Tienen este número?I'm a size 39. Do you have this size?
try something on¿Puedo probármelo?Can I try it on?
the fitting room¿Dónde están los probadores?Where are the fitting rooms?

Talla or número?

English says \"size\" for everything, but Spanish has two words. La talla is a clothing size (la 38, la M); el número is a shoe size. To give your shoe size, use calzar: calzo un 42 (I'm a size 42).

Probarse + pronoun

Probarse (to try on) is reflexive, and you know how to attach pronouns to the infinitive: ¿Puedo probármelo? (the sweater), ¿Puedo probármela? (the jacket), ¿Puedo probármelos? (the shoes). Two pronouns, so a written accent! You can also say ¿Me lo puedo probar?

Probar without a pronoun means \"to taste, to try (food)\": ¿Puedo probar el queso? And in the imperative, the salesperson will tell you: Pruébatelo (try it on).

", "

Me queda bien: the verb quedar

To say a piece of clothing \"fits well\" or \"is too big,\" Spanish uses quedar, which works like gustar: the person is an indirect pronoun, and the verb agrees with the item of clothing.

SpanishTranslation
Esta chaqueta me queda bien.This jacket looks good on me.
La falda me queda corta.The skirt is too short on me.
Estos zapatos me quedan pequeños.These shoes are too small for me.
Los pantalones te quedan largos.The pants are too long on you.
¿Qué tal me queda?How does it look on me?
Te queda genial.It looks great on you.

The adjective agrees with the item of clothing: la falda → corta, los zapatos → pequeños. Note: me queda grande already means \"it's too big for me\"; no need for \"demasiado.\"

Los pantalones is plural in Spanish, just like \"pants\" in English: Estos pantalones me quedan bien. And don't mix it up with quedar = to meet up (¿Quedamos?): the context makes it clear.

Comparing to choose

La azul me queda mejor que la negra.The blue one looks better on me than the black one.
Este jersey es más bonito, pero es carísimo.This sweater is nicer, but it's super expensive.
", "

Este, ese, aquel, then paying and exchanging

English has \"this\" and \"that.\" Spanish has three demonstratives, depending on distance:

Near me (aquí)Near you (ahí)Far from both of us (allí)
masculine singularesteeseaquel
feminine singularestaesaaquella
masculine pluralestosesosaquellos
feminine pluralestasesasaquellas
neuterestoesoaquello

The same forms work as pronouns, with no accent: Me llevo este (I'll take this one). The neuter esto, eso, aquello refers to something you don't name: ¿Qué es esto?

Careful: este ends in -e but estos ends in -os (not \"estes\"); and aquel has no -o in the masculine singular.

Paying, returning, exchanging

SpanishTranslation
¿Cómo va a pagar? / ¿Cómo vas a pagar?How would you like to pay? (usted / tú)
Con tarjeta. / En efectivo.By card. / In cash.
¿Está rebajado?Is it on sale?
Quería devolver esta camisa.I'd like to return this shirt.
¿Tiene el ticket?Do you have the receipt?
¿Me la puede cambiar por otra talla?Can you exchange it for another size?

The big sales (las rebajas) start in Spain in early January and early July: the stores go crazy!
